items.descriptionTR: In the weeks before the vote, Russia banned the import of several products from Armenia — seen as a move to heap economic pressure on the country.

items.titleTR: Armenia votes as Russia piles pressure on pro-West government

items.descriptionTR:
Voters to choose between pro-Russian opposition and incumbent Nikol Pashinyan, who is more closely aligned with the west
Armenians are awaiting the results of an election that could cement the country’s shift towards Europe and away from its traditional alliance with Russia.
Prime minister Nikol Pashinyan’s Civil Contract party entered the vote on Sunday as the favourite, ahead of three opposition candidates who advocate for closer ties with Moscow. Pashinyan’s main challenger, Samvel Karapetyan, a Russian-Armenian billionaire who built much of his fortune in Russia, was forced to campaign from house arrest at his mansion outside Yerevan.
items.titleTR: ‘It’s time to move forward’: Armenians vote in election closely watched by Russia and EU

items.descriptionTR: Armenians will decide their future on Sunday against the backdrop of a Russia-West clash, as both the EU and the US support PM Pashinyan’s cautious pro-Western drive, while Russia embarked on an onslaught of economic and political pressures on Yerevan to keep the former Soviet state in its orbit.
items.titleTR: Armenia goes to polls in pivotal vote to decide South Caucasus future

slots.packetSpot: Armenia's pivotal elections drew significant international attention, with Russia and Western countries closely monitoring the outcome. The elections were seen as a critical moment for Armenia's future direction in the South Caucasus region.
slots.packetTitle: Armenia's Pivotal Elections and Geopolitical Implications

items.descriptionTR:
Attack was ‘extremely vile’ and deliberate, says Ukraine’s president Volodymyr Zelenskyy

A Russian Shahed drone has substantially damaged a building used to store spent nuclear fuel close to the disused Chornobyl nuclear power plant, in what Ukraine’s president described as a deliberate and “extremely vile” attack.
While the structure – the reception building of the spent fuel storage facility – was empty of containers at the time, the targeting of the sensitive site appeared to be direct messaging from Moscow amid an intensifying battle of long-range aerial strikes in which high-profile locations on both sides have been hit.
items.titleTR: Russian drone hits building storing spent nuclear fuel near Chornobyl

slots.packetSpot: A Russian drone strike targeted a facility storing spent nuclear fuel near Chornobyl, raising concerns about nuclear safety in the region. The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) is monitoring the situation closely as tensions escalate.
slots.packetTitle: Russian Drone Strike on Ukrainian Nuclear Storage Facility

items.descriptionTR: A live television report from Romania's Black Sea port of Constanța was abruptly interrupted on 5 June after a maritime drone exploded nearby, heightening concerns over the regional impact of the war in Ukraine.

slots.packetSpot: A sea drone explosion occurred in Constanța port, Romania, causing significant alarm and media attention. The incident involved a Ukrainian strike on cargo ships, with Romania acknowledging the blast's impact on its territory.
slots.packetTitle: Sea Drone Explosion in Constanța Port, Romania

items.descriptionTR:
Pontiff urges followers to dedicate themselves ‘to our brothers and sisters, to the poor, to those who suffer’
More than a million people filled the streets of Madrid to join Pope Leo in an open-air mass where the American pontiff appeared to emphasise the disconnect between Christian values and far-right politics, telling worshippers: “No one can kneel before the Lord and despise their brother.”
Queues to access the mass began forming hours before the sun rose on Sunday as people scrambled to secure a spot for what was billed as the biggest gathering of the pope’s week-long visit to Spain.
items.titleTR: More than 1 million join Pope Leo for outdoor mass in Madrid

items.descriptionTR: The pontiff is set to deliver a mass in the centre of Madrid before moving elsewhere in Spain to Barcelona and the Canary islands. Pope Leo XIV is also expected to deliver an unprecedented address to the Spanish parliament, where immigration is expected to take centre stage.
items.titleTR: Pope Leo XIV calls for 'end to polarisation' as he makes the first papal visit to Spain in 15 years

slots.packetSpot: Pope Leo XIV's visit to Spain marks the first papal visit to the country in 15 years. During his visit, more than 1 million people attended an outdoor mass in Madrid, where Pope Leo XIV called for an end to political and social polarisation.
slots.packetTitle: Pope Leo XIV's Visit to Spain

items.descriptionTR:
Donald Trump says that to end the Ukraine war both sides would have to make compromises, which he took credit for suggesting without explaining further. 'I’m glad that they’re maybe talking about meeting. I think we had a lot to do with it,' Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.

	•	Zelenskyy calls for face-to-face negotiations in letter to Putin
items.titleTR: Trump says Zelenskyy-Putin meeting would be 'great' after Ukraine president's letter - video

slots.packetSpot: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has addressed an open letter to Russian President Vladimir Putin, proposing a meeting to discuss a ceasefire. Former U.S. President Donald Trump commented positively on the potential meeting, describing it as a beneficial development.
slots.packetTitle: Zelenskyy's Proposal for a Ceasefire Meeting with Putin
